_comment: GENERATED by tools/parse-map.py - do not hand-edit. Bank 5's world map: variable-length records, 24 to a row.

regions.name: World map: 807 cells, 24 per row
regions.description: 807 variable-length records in 34 rows of 24 - the world map. A record is (first byte AND $0F) + 1 bytes, stated by $8103: LDA ($16),Y / AND #$0F / SEC / ADC $16, the SEC supplying the plus one. $80F5 seeks through it counting columns to CMP #$18 and rows in $14. $8853 draws it: each qualifying cell becomes one hardware sprite at column * 4 + $10 across and row * 4 + $3B down, tile $01, attribute $03 - four pixels a cell, 96 across, a minimap. BYTE 0 bit 7 means drawn on the map and the low nibble is the length minus one; $80 exactly is an empty cell. BYTE 1's low three bits pick a progress flag - $8860 subtracts one, calls $C078 for a bit mask, ANDs with $04B0 and skips the cell when clear, which is what hides the map until you have been somewhere. BYTE 2 bit 7 marks an AREA ENTRANCE and the low seven bits are the area number. THE CHECK: the 21 records with byte 0 of $82 and byte 2 bit 7 set carry the area numbers 1 to 21, EACH EXACTLY ONCE. Twenty-one areas is what this project established from an unrelated direction - bank 4's per-area table and the CPY #$15 tests - and nothing here was tuned to produce it. The extent is checked the same way: walking the whole stream lands on $960F, the first byte of the dialogue pointer table. NOT ESTABLISHED: bits 4-6 of byte 0, and everything past byte 2 in the longer records, which run to 16 bytes. The last row holds 15 records rather than 24.
